summary: The manuscript establishes an exceptionally rigorous, mathematically complete, and formally verified (Lean 4, zero sorry) theoretical resolution to two fundamental hazards in machine-learned quantum Monte Carlo (QC-QMC) overlap surrogates: non-physical surrogate bias caused by non-holomorphicity (bar-partial f != 0) and uncertified statistical errors. It proves an elementary Grassmannian characterization of physical Slater-determinant surrogates, a universal Mixed-Energy Variational-Boost Law, Surrogate-Anchored Block Hausdorff spectral certificates verified via exact rational arithmetic (Q) LDL-transpose factorizations, and a distribution-free quantum shadow protocol with Prediction-Powered Inference (PPI) debiasing.
weaknesses: High polynomial degrees (d >= 3) in moment hierarchies face condition-number growth under exact rational LDL-transpose factorization, requiring Chebyshev or adaptive scaling.
Conservative Median-of-Means bounds require substantial shot counts (10^5-10^6) to achieve tight confidence boxes compared to heuristic baselines.
